# What PostHog personal API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is. That run is
# thirty-six characters, so a body carries it and five characters more — the
# shortest body the pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled in
# lowercase where the case does not matter and in uppercase where the case is
# what a case is about: base62 holds the letters of both, so either spelling is
# a body.

patterns: posthog-personal-api-key

# The prefix PostHog writes a personal API key with. There is a single kind of
# string here rather than a table of them: one key reads and writes the projects
# and organizations its owner can reach, within the scopes and the teams it was
# cut for, and nothing in the value says which those are. The cases below are
# that one shape in the places a key is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY=phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY=«posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header PostHog's private endpoints are called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      Authorization: Bearer «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"personal_api_key":"phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234"}
out:      {"personal_api_key":"«posthog-personal-api-key»"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234" https://us.i.posthog.com/api/projects/1/query/
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «posthog-personal-api-key»" https://us.i.posthog.com/api/projects/1/query/

case:     a key in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY": "phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234"}
out:      "env": {"POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY": "«posthog-personal-api-key»"}

# The four other prefixes PostHog writes with the same two letters. Each is a
# credential of its own and none of them is this one, so what separates them
# here is the single character behind the ph. The project API token is the one
# whose separation a caller acts on: it is published by design, written into the
# page source of every site PostHog is installed on, so it is a value a caller
# has reason to leave in a log while redacting the key beside it.

case:     a project api token
in:       phc_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phc_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     a project secret api key
in:       phs_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phs_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     an oauth access token
in:       pha_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      pha_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     an oauth refresh token
in:       phr_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phr_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

# The alphabet the body is written in. It is base62 — the letters of both cases
# and the digits — which is the wider of the two PostHog has minted a body in: a
# key minted today is base57, base62 with the five characters a reader confuses
# taken out of it, and every key minted before that is base62 and may carry any
# of the five. The two characters base64url adds, the hyphen and the underscore,
# are in neither, and either of them ends a body.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       phx_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ01234
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a body carrying the five characters base57 leaves out
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01OIl
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

# The lengths either side of forty-one. PostHog states no length for a key and
# has minted a body three ways — thirty-two random bytes in base62, then
# thirty-five, then thirty-five in base57 — each of them longer than the last, so
# the count is read as a floor rather than exactly. The floor sits below the
# shortest of the three, where what falls under it stops being something a caller
# would meet, and one character past the forty of a git SHA. What it costs is the
# second case below: a key cut short of forty-one keeps every random character
# written in front of the cut, and none of them is redacted.

case:     a body of forty-one characters is a key
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a body of forty characters is not
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123

case:     a body of the length a key is minted at today
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a run of forty ended by a hyphen with more text behind it
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123-suffix
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123-suffix

case:     a run of forty ended by an underscore with more text behind it
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123_suffix
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123_suffix

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and where
# the run of its alphabet carries on past the floor, what carries it on is
# redacted with the key. A hyphen and an underscore end the run instead.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY_phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY_«posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xphx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      x«posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234suffix
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234-suffix
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234_suffix
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234.
out:      the key is «posthog-personal-api-key».

case:     a digit before a key
in:       0phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      0«posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a hyphen before a key
in:       key-phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      key-«posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a key between japanese with nothing between them
in:       日本語phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234日本語
out:      日本語«posthog-personal-api-key»日本語

case:     a body broken by a line break
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghij\nlmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghij\nlmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     an invalid byte in the run
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\xff1234
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\xff1234

# Two keys written together. The three letters the prefix opens with belong to
# the alphabet a body is written in, so a body may close with phx and the
# underscore of the next key stand directly behind it; the second key begins
# three characters before the first one ends, the two spans overlap and are
# redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between them the first body
# reaches three characters into the second prefix and stops at the underscore
# behind them, so those two overlap as well. Written with a space between them
# the two are separate values, and both go.

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234phx_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ01234
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234 phx_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ01234
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key» «posthog-personal-api-key»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix closes with an
# underscore, which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding
# can hold one — and where forty-one base62 characters follow, the run from the
# prefix to the end of them is redacted whether or not PostHog issued it. That is
# the answer rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a key's format
# exactly and nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing these would spare
# a real key written the same way. What is taken is a stretch of a value that was
# already opaque to a reader.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzphx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234zzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzphx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234zzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«posthog-personal-api-key»

# A digest written behind the prefix, which is the one over-match here that takes
# a value a reader had a use for. Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a digest
# carries nothing that ends a run, so phx_ and the sixty-four characters of a
# SHA-256 are a key's format exactly, and both are redacted. Declining them would
# mean declining every key PostHog happened to write in the digits alone, which
# is a whole credential against a cache key. What holds either side of it is the
# floor and the prefix: a git SHA is forty characters, one short of a body, an
# MD5 is thirty-two, and a hyphen is no character the prefix carries.

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix
in:       phx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a sha256 in a cache key
in:       key: phx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «posthog-personal-api-key»

case:     a git sha behind the prefix, one character short of a body
in:       phx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      phx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       phx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      phx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha256 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       phx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      phx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, read in the
# case PostHog writes it, in the underscore it closes with and in that underscore
# being there at all. The two after them are the alphabet and the anchor: a body
# a space has broken, and a run of the right length with no prefix in front of
# it. That last one is also the shape of the keys PostHog issued before it wrote
# a prefix on any of them, which its authentication still accepts and this
# pattern cannot locate: a bare run of base62 with nothing in the text to tell it
# from an identifier.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       PHX_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      PHX_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries an underscore
in:       phx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     the prefix without its closing underscore
in:       phx0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phx0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       phx_0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      phx_0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     a key of the shape PostHog issued before it wrote a prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence
